key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: This combined coating process offers a promising route to wear-resistant surfaces on AISI 321 stainless steel components for mechanical and power engineering.
method: Deposit NiCrFeBSiC coatings by detonation spraying, then apply laser remelting.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: Before–after testing showed porosity decreasing from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness increasing from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and friction coefficient decreasing from 0.535 to 0.409.
watch_item: Corrosion current density decreased by only about 3%, so the substantial wear improvement should not be interpreted as comparable corrosion protection.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
